findings.title: Negative offsets slice the queryset, which Django rejects (or allows unsafe reads)
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes a negative cursor.offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django querysets raise an AssertionError on negative indexing, so a crafted cursor such as `0:-5:1` gives a 500 error. The comments claim the ORM handles negative slicing and that permissions are checked at the queryset level, which is false. The cursor offset comes from user input, so any admin who passes optimized_pagination=true can trigger this.

findings.title: Change to BasePaginator changes shared behavior for all paginators
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` now applies to every BasePaginator subclass. The clamp is a no-op for next-page cursors that were already validated. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is still passed through unclamped, so it fails the same way as before. The comment about "allowing negative offsets" is misleading, and the change affects all endpoints while adding no value.

findings.title: Prev-cursor trimming uses the raw offset with a different slice start
findings.body: `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` is compared against the raw cursor offset. With a negative offset, the slice length no longer corresponds to offset + limit + extra, so the extra-row trimming is wrong. Pages can then contain duplicate or missing rows.

findings.title: Authorization check may fail and exposes a hidden feature flag
findings.body: `organization_context.member` can be None, for example for a superuser who is not a member of the organization, which raises AttributeError. Because `or` short-circuits, this only happens for non-superusers. The undocumented `optimized_pagination` query parameter then enables a code path with unsafe cursor handling. Line 72 also contains trailing whitespace.

findings.title: Misleading comment; no behavior change
findings.body: The comment says negative offsets are allowed, but the code is unchanged (`int(offset)`). Negative offsets already parsed before this change, so the comment is misleading and the underlying issue is the missing validation.
